builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks via Sticky Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes
summary: This method replaces post-hoc pruning of dense networks with spike-and-slab priors and sticky PDMP samplers that set weights exactly to zero during posterior sampling. It costs substantial implementation complexity in constructing numerical rate bounds and PDMC samplers, with MCMC mixing and diagnostic overhead that likely exceeds standard training or HMC baselines. It can fail if rate bounds are incorrectly constructed or if posterior sampling fails to converge, yielding unreliable uncertainty estimates and sparse structures.
rationale: The computational and implementation burden of exact PDMC for BNNs exceeds typical 24GB GPU production budgets, and the claimed robustness benefit is not quantified for immediate adoption.
technique: Sticky PDMC sparse Bayesian neural networks

It costs substantial implementation complexity in constructing numerical rate bounds and PDMC samplers, with MCMC mixing and diagnostic overhead that likely exceeds standard training or HMC baselines. It can fail if rate bounds are incorrectly constructed or if posterior sampling fails to converge, yielding unreliable uncertainty estimates and sparse structures.
The abstract states sparse BNNs can be more robust to input noise than dense ones, but provides no quantified performance factor.
